description: We’re Thiago and Brunela, a curious and ambitious duo from Uruguay! Our interests combine digital marketing, AI, data analysis, economics, and statistics. We share a passion for critical thinking, creative problem-solving, and exploring new challenges. Although we don't have a programming background, we're eager to learn, experiment with technology, and turn innovative ideas into meaningful solutions. We're excited to push our limits and make the most of this NASA challenge!
summary: Mars Before Mars proposes a Mars analog site in the Desierto del Diablo, near Tolar Grande, Salta, Argentina (24.50° S, 67.15° W, 3,800 m). We used NASA POWER climate data, NASA SRTM terrain data and the real path of NASA's Perseverance rover to test how well the site matches Mars. The median slope of our Salta plain is 3.0%, against 2.8% along the rover's 708 recorded positions in Jezero crater. On that site we propose something that has never been tested: a society. 100 volunteers would live for 26 months in a dome town under Mars rules, including delayed messages to Earth. What we learn about how they live, work, decide and care for each other redesigns the dome, so version 2 reaches Mars built to last, without avoidable costs or mistakes. We built a bilingual website with an interactive 3D tour of the dome, a 3D model of the real terrain and live Earth to Mars data, plus a 30 second film.
details:
WHAT IT IS

A proposal for a Mars analog in the Puna of Salta, Argentina, and for the first long experiment with a full community instead of a small crew. Past analogs tested 4 to 6 trained people (Mars-500, NASA CHAPEA). A settlement will be a society, and nobody has tested one.

HOW WE CHOSE AND TESTED THE PLACE

Climate: NASA POWER gives a mean air temperature of 3.1 °C, a mean day to night swing of 15.7 °C and 39% mean relative humidity for the site. It is cold, dry and has large thermal swings.

Terrain: we computed slopes from NASA SRTM 30 m elevation data along sample transects on the Salta plain and compared them with the slopes between the 708 waypoints of the Perseverance rover (sols 13 to 2022). Median slope: 3.0% in Salta, 2.8% on the rover path.

Limits, stated openly: Earth gravity, air pressure and radiation still apply. The rover followed a chosen path and our sample is a straight transect, so similar medians do not prove identical terrain.

THE EXPERIMENT

100 volunteers aged 21 to 45 live for 26 months in a dome town. Messages to Earth are delayed up to 20 minutes. With consent, researchers follow leadership, work and resources, mood and sleep, and conflict. Volunteers can leave at any time, with confidential support.

THE GOAL AND THE IMPACT

Every result maps to a design change: private space, shared rooms, rules, supplies. Dome version 1 is our best guess. Dome version 2 is rebuilt from how 100 people really lived, so mistakes are found on Earth, where fixing them is still cheap, and the domes that reach Mars are built to last for years.

WHAT WE BUILT

A bilingual website (English and Spanish) with an interactive 3D tour of the dome, a 3D model of the real terrain, the rover path comparison, live Earth to Mars distance and signal delay, and a 30 second film.

WHY IT IS CREATIVE

It treats the settlement as a social problem, not only an engineering one, and it uses a rover's real path as the yardstick for an Earth site.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, three.js, Python.

USE OF AI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE) TOOLS

Code and data: the website code and the data analysis scripts were written with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic). All data values come from the NASA and partner sources listed below, not from AI.

Text: the texts of the website, slides and this form were written and edited with AI assistance (Claude).

Images: the concept images of the dome were generated with AI (ChatGPT) and carry a visible "AI generated concept" label on the website and in the video. The 3D model is labeled "Conceptual 3D model".

Video and audio: the animation of the demo video was made with AI assistance (Claude). The narrator voice, music and sound effects were generated with AI (ElevenLabs). This is stated on screen in the video and in the file metadata.

No NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers appear in any AI generated content.
